```{r setup}
#| include: false
# Alle Pfade relativ zum Projektordner, nicht zum Ordner reports/
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
```

```{r load-data}
#| include: false
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

source("scripts/read_hh.R")

# Beim ersten Mal alle Türme einlesen und als .rds zwischenspeichern,
# danach geht das Rendern viel schneller.
cache_file <- "data/processed/all_hh.rds"
if (file.exists(cache_file)) {
  all_hh <- readRDS(cache_file)
} else {
  zips   <- list.files("data/raw", pattern = "\\.zip$", full.names = TRUE)
  all_hh <- bind_rows(lapply(zips, read_hh))
  saveRDS(all_hh, cache_file)
}

snapshot_file <- list.files("data/snapshots", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)[1]
snapshot      <- read_csv(snapshot_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## C1. Site overview

The five towers were downloaded with the FLUXNET Shuttle. The snapshot file
`r basename(snapshot_file)` records what was downloaded. The data files are:
`r paste(basename(list.files("data/raw", pattern = "\\.zip$")), collapse = ", ")`.

```{r c1-table}
my_sites  <- sort(unique(all_hh$site))
countries <- c(BR = "Brazil", CN = "China", IT = "Italy", JP = "Japan", US = "USA")

sites <- snapshot |>
  filter(site_id %in% my_sites) |>
  distinct(site_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(country = countries[substr(site_id, 1, 2)])

sites |>
  select(`Site ID` = site_id, Name = site_name, Country = country, IGBP = igbp,
         `Lat (°)` = location_lat, `Lon (°)` = location_long,
         `First year` = first_year, `Last year` = last_year,
         Hub = data_hub, Citation = product_citation) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

```{r c1-map}
#| fig-cap: "Location of the five flux towers."
world <- map_data("world")

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = world, aes(long, lat, group = group),
               fill = "grey90", colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_point(data = sites, aes(location_long, location_lat),
             colour = "red", size = 3) +
  geom_text(data = sites, aes(location_long, location_lat, label = site_id),
            nudge_y = 7, size = 3.5) +
  coord_quickmap() +
  labs(x = "Longitude (°)", y = "Latitude (°)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

**Variables used.** NEE, GPP and RECO are the `_REF` products. Where available,
the variable u* threshold (VUT) and night-time partitioning (NT) were used.
Where these were empty, the constant u* threshold (CUT) or day-time
partitioning (DT) was used instead:

```{r c1-variables}
all_hh |>
  distinct(Site = site, `u* threshold` = ustar, Partitioning = partition) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

Time stamps are local standard time (no daylight saving). They are stored with
`tz = "UTC"` only as a technical container.


## C2. Data coverage

Share of half hours per site and year in which NEE was measured
(`NEE_QC == 0`) and not gap-filled.

```{r c2-coverage}
#| fig-cap: "Share of measured (not gap-filled) NEE half hours per site and year."
#| fig-height: 3.5
coverage <- all_hh |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(format(time, "%Y"))) |>
  summarise(measured = mean(NEE_QC %in% 0), .by = c(site, year))

ggplot(coverage, aes(year, site, fill = measured)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Measured NEE", labels = scales::percent,
                       limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Site") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r c2-best}
#| include: false
best      <- coverage |> slice_max(measured, n = 1)
site_mean <- coverage |> summarise(measured = mean(measured), .by = site) |>
  arrange(desc(measured))
```

The best data come from `r site_mean$site[1]` (on average
`r round(100 * site_mean$measured[1])` % measured NEE per year); the single best
site-year is `r best$site` in `r best$year` (`r round(100 * best$measured)` %). BR-Ma2 has the lowest share of measured NEE, espacially in the first half of recorded years

## C3. Summary statistics

Mean, minimum, maximum and share of missing half hours for each site. For
precipitation (P_F), the *Mean* row gives the **mean annual sum** (mm per year);
Min and Max of P_F refer to half-hourly values.

```{r c3-stats}
#| results: asis
vars <- c(TA_F     = "TA_F (°C)",
          SW_IN_F  = "SW_IN_F (W m⁻²)",
          VPD_F    = "VPD_F (hPa)",
          P_F      = "P_F (mm)",
          NEE      = "NEE (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)",
          GPP      = "GPP (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)",
          RECO     = "RECO (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)",
          H_F_MDS  = "H (W m⁻²)",
          LE_F_MDS = "LE (W m⁻²)")

# Statistiken für alle Variablen und Türme
stats <- all_hh |>
  select(site, all_of(names(vars))) |>
  pivot_longer(-site, names_to = "var") |>
  summarise(Mean        = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Min         = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Max         = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            `% missing` = 100 * mean(is.na(value)),
            .by = c(site, var))

# Niederschlag: mittlere Jahressumme statt Mittelwert
p_annual <- all_hh |>
  mutate(year = format(time, "%Y")) |>
  summarise(p_sum = sum(P_F, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(site, year)) |>
  summarise(p_annual = mean(p_sum), .by = site)

stats <- stats |>
  left_join(p_annual, by = "site") |>
  mutate(Mean = if_else(var == "P_F", p_annual, Mean)) |>
  select(-p_annual)

# Eine Tabelle pro Turm
for (s in my_sites) {
  cat("\n\n### ", s, "\n\n", sep = "")
  tab <- stats |>
    filter(site == s) |>
    select(-site) |>
    mutate(var = vars[var]) |>
    pivot_longer(c(Mean, Min, Max, `% missing`), names_to = "Statistic") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = var, values_from = value)
  cat(knitr::kable(tab, digits = 1), sep = "\n")
}
```
**Note on precipitation.** At US-UiB and CN-Zha, P_F is identical to the ERA5
reanalysis (P_ERA) in every year, i.e. no precipitation was measured at these
towers and the whole record is gap-filled from ERA5. The annual sums are
roughly four times higher than the regional climate (about 1,000 mm in central
Illinois and 100–200 mm around Zhangye). To rule out an error in my own
aggregation, I compared my annual sums from the half-hourly data with the
annual files of the data product:

```{r c3-precip-check}
p_compare <- lapply(c("US-UiB", "CN-Zha"), function(s) {
  z     <- list.files("data/raw", pattern = paste0(s, ".*\\.zip$"), full.names = TRUE)
  files <- unzip(z, list = TRUE)$Name
  era <- read_csv(unz(z, grep("ERA5_YY", files, value = TRUE)),
                  na = "-9999", show_col_types = FALSE)
  yy  <- read_csv(unz(z, grep("FLUXMET_YY", files, value = TRUE)),
                  na = "-9999", show_col_types = FALSE)
  tibble(Site = s,
         `Own sum from HH (mm yr⁻¹)` = p_annual$p_annual[p_annual$site == s],
         `FLUXMET_YY P_F (mm yr⁻¹)`  = mean(yy$P_F, na.rm = TRUE),
         `ERA5_YY P_ERA (mm yr⁻¹)`   = mean(era$P_ERA[era$TIMESTAMP %in% yy$TIMESTAMP],
                                            na.rm = TRUE))
})
bind_rows(p_compare) |> knitr::kable(digits = 0)
```

All three values agree, and the half-hourly files contain 48 time steps per day
(17,520 or 17,568 per year). The overestimation is therefore not caused by my
aggregation but is already present in the data product (ERA5-based P_F).
P_F at these two sites is not interpreted further. At BR-Ma2, IT-Tor and
JP-Fhk, P_F is close to ERA5 and in a plausible range.

## C4. Time series

Daily values were aggregated from the half-hourly data as the daily mean
(µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹) and converted to g C m⁻² d⁻¹ with the factor 1.0378
(86 400 s × 12.011 g mol⁻¹ × 10⁻⁶). Days with missing half hours are left empty.

```{r c4-daily}
daily <- all_hh |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(time)) |>
  summarise(across(c(NEE, GPP, RECO), ~ mean(.x) * 1.0378),
            .by = c(site, date))
```

```{r c4-plot}
#| fig-cap: "Daily NEE, GPP and RECO for each site."
#| fig-height: 11
daily |>
  pivot_longer(c(NEE, GPP, RECO), names_to = "flux") |>
  ggplot(aes(date, value, colour = flux)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ site, ncol = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(GPP = "darkgreen", RECO = "darkorange", NEE = "black")) +
  labs(x = "Date", y = "Daily flux (g C m⁻² d⁻¹)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

### Check against the daily FLUXMET_DD file

```{r c4-check}
#| fig-cap: "Own daily NEE aggregation vs. the official FLUXMET_DD file (JP-Fhk)."
#| fig-height: 4
z       <- list.files("data/raw", pattern = "JP-Fhk.*\\.zip$", full.names = TRUE)
dd_name <- grep("FLUXMET_DD", unzip(z, list = TRUE)$Name, value = TRUE)

dd <- read_csv(unz(z, dd_name), na = "-9999",
               col_select = c(TIMESTAMP, NEE_VUT_REF),
               col_types = cols(TIMESTAMP = "c", .default = "d")) |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(TIMESTAMP, format = "%Y%m%d"))

cmp <- daily |>
  filter(site == "JP-Fhk") |>
  inner_join(dd, by = "date")

ggplot(cmp, aes(NEE_VUT_REF, NEE)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "red") +
  labs(x = "NEE from FLUXMET_DD (g C m⁻² d⁻¹)",
       y = "Own daily NEE (g C m⁻² d⁻¹)") +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_minimal()
```

For JP-Fhk, the own aggregation agrees with the official daily file:
r = `r round(cor(cmp$NEE, cmp$NEE_VUT_REF, use = "complete.obs"), 4)`,
mean absolute difference = `r signif(mean(abs(cmp$NEE - cmp$NEE_VUT_REF), na.rm = TRUE), 2)` g C m⁻² d⁻¹.

## C5. Diurnal cycles

Seasons were defined from the month and the latitude of each site. In the
northern hemisphere, spring is March–May, summer June–August, autumn
September–November and winter December–February. For sites with a negative
latitude (here only BR-Ma2), the months were shifted by six months, so that
for example January counts as summer. BR-Ma2 lies almost on the equator
(`r abs(round(sites$location_lat[sites$site_id == "BR-Ma2"], 1))`° S), so its
"seasons" are weak and mainly reflect wet and dry periods. Hours are local
standard time (start of the half hour).

```{r c5-diurnal}
#| fig-cap: "Mean diurnal cycle of NEE and LE per season for all five sites."
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 10
season_nh <- c("Winter", "Winter", "Spring", "Spring", "Spring", "Summer",
               "Summer", "Summer", "Autumn", "Autumn", "Autumn", "Winter")

diurnal <- all_hh |>
  left_join(sites |> select(site = site_id, lat = location_lat), by = "site") |>
  mutate(month  = as.integer(format(time, "%m")),
         # Südhalbkugel: Monate um 6 verschieben (Januar -> Juli usw.)
         month_adj = if_else(lat < 0, (month + 5) %% 12 + 1, month),
         season = factor(season_nh[month_adj],
                         levels = c("Spring", "Summer", "Autumn", "Winter")),
         hour   = as.numeric(format(time, "%H")) + as.numeric(format(time, "%M")) / 60) |>
  summarise(`NEE (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹)` = mean(NEE, na.rm = TRUE),
            `LE (W m⁻²)`             = mean(LE_F_MDS, na.rm = TRUE),
            .by = c(site, season, hour))

diurnal |>
  pivot_longer(-c(site, season, hour), names_to = "variable") |>
  ggplot(aes(hour, value, colour = site)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(variable ~ season, scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, 6)) +
  labs(x = "Hour of day (local standard time)", y = NULL, colour = "Site") +
  theme_minimal(base_size=13) +
  theme(strip.placement = "outside", legend.position = "top")
```

## C6. My reading

### Energy balance (JP-Fhk)

Only half hours in which both H and LE were measured (`_QC == 0`) are used.

```{r c6-energy}
#| fig-cap: "Energy balance at JP-Fhk: turbulent fluxes vs. available energy (measured half hours only)."
#| fig-height: 5
eb <- all_hh |>
  filter(site == "JP-Fhk", H_F_MDS_QC == 0, LE_F_MDS_QC == 0) |>
  mutate(available = NETRAD - G_F_MDS,
         turbulent = H_F_MDS + LE_F_MDS) |>
  filter(!is.na(available), !is.na(turbulent))

fit   <- lm(turbulent ~ available, data = eb)
slope <- coef(fit)[["available"]]

ggplot(eb, aes(available, turbulent)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.3, alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "blue", se = FALSE) +
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.5,
           label = paste0("slope = ", round(slope, 2), " (n = ", nrow(eb), ")")) +
  labs(x = "NETRAD − G (W m⁻²)", y = "H + LE (W m⁻²)") +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

The slope of the linear fit is `r round(slope, 2)` (red line: 1:1).

### Comparison of the towers

```{r c6-numbers}
# Jährliche NEE-Summe: µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ × 1800 s × 12.011e-6 g/µmol = g C pro Halbstunde
annual <- all_hh |>
  mutate(year = format(time, "%Y")) |>
  summarise(nee_sum = sum(NEE * 1800 * 12.011e-6), .by = c(site, year)) |>
  filter(!is.na(nee_sum)) |>                       # nur vollständige Jahre
  summarise(`Mean annual NEE (g C m⁻² yr⁻¹)` = mean(nee_sum),
            `Complete years` = n(), .by = site)

# Jahresgang: Spannweite der mittleren monatlichen GPP (Tageswerte aus C4)
seasonal <- daily |>
  mutate(month = format(date, "%m")) |>
  summarise(gpp = mean(GPP, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(site, month)) |>
  summarise(`GPP seasonal amplitude (g C m⁻² d⁻¹)` = max(gpp) - min(gpp), .by = site)

# Anteil lückengefüllter NEE-Halbstunden
gapfilled <- all_hh |>
  summarise(`Gap-filled NEE (%)` = 100 * mean(!(NEE_QC %in% 0)), .by = site)

annual |>
  left_join(seasonal, by = "site") |>
  left_join(gapfilled, by = "site") |>
  rename(Site = site) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

The highest carbon uptake occurs at the Illinois tower (US-UiB), which surprised
me, considering that one of my towers is located in the Amazon rainforest. This
could partly be explained by the high share of gap-filled NEE values at the
Manaus tower (76 %) and the fact that only seven complete years are available
there. What seems to be the highest carbon uptake is not nessesarily a proxy for the highest productivity because its cropland and the carbon (fruits) get harvested. US-UiB also shows the largest seasonal cycle in GPP. The lowest carbon
uptake occurs at the tower in the Aosta Valley (IT-Tor), which could be explained
by the short growing season at high altitude. At JP-Fhk, the turbulent fluxes
(H + LE) account for about `r round(100 * slope)` % of the available energy
(slope = `r round(slope, 2)`), so the energy balance is not fully closed.

Note that GPP and RECO at BR-Ma2 come from the day-time partitioning (DT),
while all other sites use the night-time method (NT). The two methods can
give different GPP and RECO, so the comparison of BR-Ma2 with the other
sites is less direct.

## Data and citation

**Site data.** Each site's data citation, taken from the snapshot file
`r basename(snapshot_file)`:

```{r citations}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
cat(paste0("- **", sites$site_id, "**: ", sites$product_citation), sep = "\n")
```

**FLUXNET processing.** Pastorello, G. et al. (2020): The FLUXNET2015 dataset
and the ONEFlux processing pipeline for eddy covariance data. *Scientific Data*
7, 225. <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-020-0534-3>

**Data products.** FLUXNET data products (ONEFlux v1.3), downloaded with the
FLUXNET Shuttle from AmeriFlux and the ICOS Carbon Portal. Licence: CC-BY-4.0.
